ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary authority: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50-2 and R.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Articles L.561-45 to L.561-46 and R.561-56 to R.561-57 creating the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE) maintained by the commercial court registry (greffe) and relayed through the INPI; Décret n° 2020-118 of 12 February 2020 and Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 reforming company law formalities and the single electronic portal (guichet unique); Loi n° 2016-1691 of 1 December 2016 (Sapin II) on transparency and anti-corruption; Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code (Code de commerce) on RCS registration and the constitution of the Société par Actions Simplifiée under Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 and R.210-1 to R.210-21. Following CJEU judgments C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 November 2022, public access to the French RBE is restricted to competent authorities, obliged entities performing statutory customer due diligence, and applicants demonstrating a legitimate interest; default access therefore rests with governmental authorities and regulated professionals.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation (or equivalent foreign registry extract) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or official corporate registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille pursuant to the HCCH Convention of 5 October 1961 if the origin country is a Contracting State; otherwise full French Consular Legalization by the Consular Section of the French Embassy in the origin country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and tax residence certificate of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority or registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization as applicable under the country of origin law

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (procuration) empowering the incorporation agent, legal counsel, or appointed SAS President
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or designated legalization authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization; certified French translation by an approved court interpreter required for filing with the greffe

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport and identity document copies of all shareholders, UBOs, and the proposed SAS President
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public, passport issuing authority, or prefecture in each country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization of the notarized attestation, accompanied by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank adoption letter or KYC banking reference letter supporting the SWIFT wire and letter of credit payment rails
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution or correspondent bank of the shareholder or the future SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank seal authentication legalized via Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as required by the receiving French credit institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every shareholder, officer, alternate beneficial owner and signatory against: (i) the consolidated EU financial sanctions list implemented by the French Treasury (ASTRAC), including EU Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001, EU Regulation 269/2010 and EU Regulation 267/2012 asset-freeze measures; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) French preventive measures and TRACFIN typology notices; and (iv) OFAC's SDN List, applied as enhanced due diligence market practice for USD SWIFT wire settlement. Politically Exposed Person identification is mandatory under Article R.561-18 of the Code monétaire et financier, covering heads of state, senior politicians, senior judicial and military officials, senior state representatives, members of supervisory boards of state bodies, and family members or close associates of such persons; any positive match triggers enhanced due diligence (EDD) and, where required, a written report to TRACFIN. KYS (Know Your Signatory) verification, corruption indicators, sanctions-tie-breaker analysis, and source-of-funds documentation must be archived in a pre-incorporation CDD file with a retained audit trail for submission to the banking counterparty and the professional association registering the entity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, with entry in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) effected by the territorially competent greffe du tribunal de commerce and public index accessible via Infogreffe
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be drafted in Latin script. Loi n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (Toubon Law) and Article L.123-1-1 of the Code de commerce require that mandatory company documentation addressed to the French public be in French; therefore any foreign-language name must be transliterated into Latin characters and a French-language descriptive subtitle is recommended. The name must not contain misleading numerals, must include the corporate form suffix SAS or the full form Société par Actions Simplifiée in all public documents, and must comply with public policy, social order and bonos mores.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque and banking terms, requiring prior authorization of the ACPR under Articles L.511-1 and L.522-1 of the Code monétaire et financier
Assurance and insurance terms, requiring prior ACPR authorization under the French Insurance Code
Fiduciaire, Fonds, Gestion de patrimoine and asset-management tokens requiring AMF or ACPR clearance
French public authority terms: République, Ministère, Préfecture, Police, Gendarmerie, Mairie, État
Terms implying a regulated profession: Avocat, Notaire, Expert-Comptable, Commissaire aux Comptes
Misleading terms suggesting European Union institutional status, official certification, or accredited standards bodies (e.g., ISO, CEN)
Terms contrary to public decency, Sapin II anti-corruption rules, or EU and UN sanctions obligations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection by the greffier or the INPI issued through the guichet unique, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal (recours gracieux) with the INPI within 15 days of notification, requesting reconsideration with corrected or supplementary documentation. If the refusal is confirmed, the applicant may lodge a judicial appeal before the President of the territorially competent Tribunal de Commerce (or the Tribunal Judiciaire for decisions affecting the RBE) exercising summary jurisdiction (référé) within one month of the rejection notification, pursuant to Articles R.123-4 and R.123-5 et seq. of the Code de commerce and the guichet unique implementing regulation. The appeal file must evidence priority of the earlier filing, an INPI Direct trademark clearance certificate, and, where a forbidden term is concerned, the prior ministerial authorization letter. Where the rejection arises from trademark conflict, a coexistence agreement or opposition procedure under Article L.712-4 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle may be filed with the INPI within two months of publication.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible through a written domiciliation agreement with an approved commercial domiciliation company under Article L.123-11-1 of the Code de commerce; the agreement must be concluded for a minimum of one year, is renewable, and may be terminated on three months' notice. For the fabless semiconductor design and IP core licensing business, a domiciliated virtual registered office is accepted at inception; however, commercial substance for French tax residence, French VAT enforcement, and future R&D relief requires that management decisions, statutory books and registers (registre des décisions de l'associé unique, registre des mouvements de titres), books and records, and contractual records of IP licenses be physically accessible in France. A physical operating space or an authorized data-room address is strongly advised before claiming the French research tax credit (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche), patent box treatment, or any transfer-pricing IP equalization arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 15-25% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 24 months of registration, rising to approximately 40% where the company declares tax losses, claims research tax credits, or receives substantial IP royalty flows in the first two fiscal years. Inspections may be performed by DGFiP tax auditors (including searches under Article L.16 B of the Livre des procédures fiscales), URSSAF social security inspectors upon the first employee hire, and commercial court greffe random verification of registered office effectiveness. A domiciliation agreement does not eliminate inspection risk; under Article L.210-2 of the Code de commerce, the registered office must be effective for service of process, receipt of official correspondence, and preservation of the company's statutory archive.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official regulated greffe tariff (tarif réglementé des greffiers de commerce), approximately EUR 76.70 plus portal administration charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff band and prevailing market benchmark ranging EUR 185-225 per publication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cour d'appel statutory rate card, per-document and per-page certified translation rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certification of foreign-origin documents (shareholder incorporation certificate, good standing certificate, notarized passport copies, power of attorney, and bank reference letter)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark annual package, standard range EUR 300-600

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Code de commerce: Articles L.210-1 et seq. (general company law), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-27 (Société par Actions Simplifiée), Articles R.123-1 et seq. and Décret n°84-406 (registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés / Registre National des Entreprises); Order 2023-393 and related RNE provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office, accessed through the INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 / Demande d'immatriculation d'une personne morale au RNE, filed together with the statuts constitutifs of the SAS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS. If share capital is subscribed in cash, at least 50% of such cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation and the balance within five years or within the shorter period fixed in the statuts. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up and, where applicable, reviewed by a contribution auditor. No statutory escrow account is required, but cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked account with a French credit institution and evidenced by a bank certificate before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders of the SAS [Company] approve and adopt the articles of association and subscribe in full to the share capital represented by [number] shares as set out in the capital table; all cash contributions have been paid up to the statutory minimum and in-kind contributions have been duly valued. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [address], France; the President is authorized to sign the lease, open the bank account and complete the incorporation filing. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed as Président of the SAS for a three-year term, with the powers provided by law and the articles of association, and any other officers required under the bylaws are appointed. Each appointee accepts office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders in private writing; notarial execution optional but required if real-property contributions are made or the shareholders elect a notarial deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare final French-language statuts for the SAS, including corporate name, registered office, corporate object covering integrated-circuit architecture design and IP core licensing, share capital, share classes, duration, management structure, powers of the President and decision-making rules. Each shareholder signs the statuts; if in-kind contributions are made, appoint a commissaire aux apports where required by law.
required_dossiers: Final statuts constitutifs of the SAS
Shareholders' identity documents or corporate extracts
Declaration of beneficial owners
Contribution valuation report, if in-kind contributions exist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Hold a rectification meeting and execute a supplementary deed if a signature or clause is defective; if the notary refuses, correct the deed or convert it to a private signed deed where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the corporate bank account and block cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution chosen by the shareholders or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the SAS in formation. Transfer the agreed cash contributions and block the funds until the company is registered. Obtain the bank's attestation de blocage de fonds or certificat du dépositaire proving the deposit.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts
Shareholders' identity documents
Anti-money-laundering and KYC forms
Bank account opening form and deposit receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected attestation if the bank certificate is inaccurate; if the bank unreasonably refuses service, re-register the block through Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or choose another licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Publication support d'annonces légales authorized in the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Insert the required incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in a duly authorized legal-announcement journal. The notice must mention the company name, SAS form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration and details of the person authorised to act. Obtain the attestation de parution for inclusion in the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Text of the draft legal announcement
Proof of payment of publication fees
Details of the registered office and President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected certificate from the journal if the notice contains errors; if the chosen journal is not valid, select an authorized journal and re-publish before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 registration request online, upload the executed statuts, registered-office proof, bank blockage certificate, legal-announcement certificate, identity documents of the President, declaration of non-conviction and beneficial-owner declaration. Pay the filing fees and submit the dossier for legal review.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 / RNE application form
Signed statuts constitutifs
Bank certificate of blocked funds
Attestation de parution of the legal announcement
Proof of the registered office address
Identity document of the President
Declaration of non-conviction if required
Declaration of beneficial owners
Proof of payment of official fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Guichet Unique may issue a demande de régularisation requiring missing or corrective documents; cure the dossier within 15 days. If the Greffe refuses the registration, resubmit a cured dossier or apply to the Président of the commercial court for judicial authorization to register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Kbis extract and registration identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI Registre National des Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the dossier is accepted, the company is registered and issued an extract Kbis evidencing legal existence, SIREN/SIRET numbers and APE/NAF code 2610Z. Verify that all particulars are correct and retain the RNE registration receipt.
required_dossiers: Electronic receipt of the registration dossier
Kbis extract issued by the Greffe
Confirmation of SIREN/SIRET and APE code
Registered-office proof and manager details as recorded
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis shows an error in company data or APE code, file an application for rectification with the Greffe; if the registry omits a required mention, request a supplementary registration or seek judicial rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration social and tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, Direction Générale des Finances Publiques, and local authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SAS as an employer, complete the DPAE for each employee, verify corporate income tax status, choose or confirm the financial year, register for applicable local business taxes and ensure the register of shareholder decisions and share transfers is established.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
DPAE employee declarations
Corporate tax questionnaire and financial-year election
Register of shareholder decisions and share registers
Lease or ownership title for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late declarations are cured by spontaneous regularization; contact URSSAF and the tax administration to agree on payment timelines and request reduction of late-filing penalties where good faith is shown.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Entreprises, Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement for environmental matters, and Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects / SGDSN for dual-use technology export controls
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate French industrial operating permit is required for a fabless semiconductor design office, because the activity is non-classified and does not constitute an installation classée. The Kbis/RNE registration is the primary authorization to operate; if technology or integrated-circuit IP covered by EU dual-use controls is transferred, an authorization under Regulation (EU) 2021/821 and the French Code de la défense may be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) of the region of the registered office, under the Préfet de région
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Non-ICPE: the activity is a tertiary design and licensing service, not a manufacturing plant; no EIA report or environmental authorization is required unless a clean-room, pilot fabrication line or chemical-based laboratory is subsequently added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, process VOC emissions or hazardous waste streams arise from pure fabless design. Any future pilot line must comply with the Code de l'environnement ICPE thresholds and Directive 2010/75/EU; office waste must be sorted and recovered under Articles L.541-1 et seq. of the Code de l'environnement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety attestation of the building owner or ERP category-5 compliance if the premises are open to public; structural load-bearing attestation for equipment rooms; electrical installation inspection certificate; workplace health-and-safety compliance under Article L.4121-1 of the Code du travail, including a single risk-assessment document, emergency evacuation planning, disabled-access compliance, company medical service and occupational accident insurance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – official portal: impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity forming a French SAS initiates registration through the single business formalities portal at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Upon completion of immatriculation at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, the DGFiP assigns the SIREN/SIRET statutory identifiers. The VAT identification number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) is issued subsequently by the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises, with EORI registration required for intra-EU/export customs operations. The corporate tax file is activated automatically with the SIRET, and the SAS must file an initial results declaration under its corporate income tax regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French tax law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. A SAS is mandatorily subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at entity level. Available statutory elections include fiscal group integration under CGI Article 223 A et seq., VAT grouping under CGI Article 1693 ter (assujetti unique), and the reduced corporate tax rate for small and medium-sized enterprises under CGI Article 219 when statutory conditions are met.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise en base thresholds for domestic micro-businesses: EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services. However, foreign/non-resident suppliers have no threshold and must register for French VAT immediately upon making any taxable supply in France unless the transaction is outside scope or subject to reverse charge under CGI Article 194.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured electronic invoicing and e-reporting to DGFiP through a certified Partner Dematerialisation Platform (PDP) or the public Chorus Pro portal, phased from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and 1 September 2027 for small and medium-sized enterprises. France does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system; transmission of invoice data occurs at issuance, with VAT settlement via Form CA3/3310 through the DGFiP electronic filing system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically removed from France to destinations outside the European Union qualify for 0% VAT under CGI Article 262-I-1°, provided transport evidence demonstrates actual exit of the goods within 90 days of dispatch. Semiconductor IP core licensing and fabless design services supplied to recipients established outside France are outside French VAT scope under the B2B place-of-supply rules (CGI Article 259-2 and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC), allowing zero-rate treatment. Intra-Union B2B supplies of semiconductor licenses can also be zero-rated when the customer's valid EU VAT number is obtained and recapitulative statements are filed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/ENS – Document Administratif Unique)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing physical removal from the EU
Commercial invoice and signed export order
Inward Remittance Certificate proving foreign currency payment from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP applies heightened audit scrutiny to export zero-rating claims. Failure to substantiate the physical export and receipt of payment within the required documentation and 180-day FX repatriation period triggers reinstatement of the 20% VAT with late interest (intérêts de retard). Penalties escalate from 40% for material under-declaration (insuffisance de déclaration) to 80% for deliberate misconduct (manquement délibéré) or concealed activity (exercice occulte). Forgery or falsification of export and customs documents constitutes tax fraud, exposing the SAS and its directors to criminal fines and imprisonment under the French General Tax Code and Customs Code clawback mechanisms.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) acting jointly with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) and the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) for foreign-exchange statistical, balance-of-payments and exchange-control surveillance, in accordance with the French Monetary and Financial Code and Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union Articles 63-66.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full euro-zone convertibility applies. Both capital and current-account transactions are liberalised under EU capital-movement rules; no currency inconvertibility or exchange-approval restriction exists for the French SAS. Profit remittance (dividends) is unrestricted subject to AML/KYC verification, potential French withholding tax (30% standard flat tax on outbound dividends, reducible to 15%/5% under applicable double-tax treaties, or 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the shareholder qualifies), and Banque de France statistical direct-investment declarations. Fabless IP-core royalty receipts are classified as current-account business revenue and are freely repatriable without convertibility, licensing or prior-exchange-approval hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export receivables may be retained in any foreign currency. However, French resident corporate exporters are required to file balance-of-payments statistical declarations with the Banque de France for direct investment flows where the transaction or cumulative external position exceeds the €15,000,000 threshold, and ongoing external financial-account declarations apply to foreign receivables above de minimis levels; USD invoicing for semiconductor IP licences is expressly permitted.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Commercial Operational Current Account (Compte Courant Professionnel) and Blocked Capital Subscription Account (Compte Bloqué)
Commercial Operational Current Account and Blocked Capital Subscription Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank / Crédit Agricole LCL
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Commercial Operational Current Account with Documentary Credit and Trade-Finance Desks
Commercial Operational Current Account with Export Trade-Finance Services
Commercial Operational Current Account with Cross-Border FX and Correspondent Banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (e.g., French-authorised Qonto or passporting EU EMIs such as Revolut Business) may support day-to-day euro operational liquidity, SEPA/SEPA Instant transfers, FX conversion and payment cards under the French Monetary and Financial Code. They are, however, not viable as the sole treasury backbone for a fabless semiconductor treasury requiring USD correspondent banking, Commercial Letters of Credit, documentary collections, or ACPR-regulated credit and hedging lines. Non-EU EMIs (e.g., UK or US-based providers) receive a Low viability rating because of French client-money segregation rules, the absence of French IBAN compensation, and bank-in-the-middle KYC frictions for recurring high-value trade flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law (CMF Article R.561-16-1, transposing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849) allows remote video KYC identification, but tier-1 French banks generally maintain a de facto physical interview mandate for signatories, beneficial owners and directors residing outside the EEA. For a French SAS with non-French resident directors, a physical onboarding meeting in France is effectively mandatory for at least one person holding actual signature authority; fully remote account opening is viable only for EEA-resident natural persons with electronically verifiable identity documents, and in such cases an apostilled, sworn-translated, notarised KYC dossier is required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and a non-French SAS President attempting a non-face-to-face account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) certified by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; certified passports and EEA proofs of residence for all UBOs; corporate authorisations (Pouvoirs) and notarised board resolutions; apostilled and sworn-translated constitutional documents (Statuts); source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; bank reference letters from the remitting foreign institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: High-value IP royalty and licence-fee flows booked against the French corporate tax base, raising transfer-pricing and base-erosion exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD-aligned transfer-pricing documentation (Master File and French Local File); independent valuation report for the fabless IP cores (relief-from-royalty or discounted-cash-flow method); executed licence agreements with arm's-length royalty rates; documented intercompany substance and economic analysis; correspondence with the French tax administration (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) confirming the tax treatment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Cross-border disbursements to foundries, subcontractors and US/Asia trading counterparties, including possible exposure to consolidated sanctions or high-risk third-country jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU consolidated sanctions screening results; dual-use export-control licence where applicable under EU Regulation 2021/821; commercial invoices and harmonised-system tariff classifications; supply-chain traceability evidence; FATF risk-rated counterparty due-diligence files; signed compliance attestations from the French SAS compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Large inbound capital injection from a non-EU investor in the semiconductor design sector, triggering French Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prior authorisation file under French Décret n° 2019-1590 and EU Regulation 2019/452 where the non-EU investor acquires control or more than 25% of voting rights in a sensitive semiconductor-technology entity; executed shareholders' agreement and capital-increase resolution; documentary evidence tracing the onward source of funds; declaration of funds exceeding €10,000 in cash where relevant; bank references from the remitting institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire-transfer routing for inbound equity or shareholder-loan injections uses SWIFT MT103 for cross-border currencies or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR, with mandatory ISO 20022/EPC purpose codes. Equity subscription transfers must be tagged with the EU Balance-of-Payments direct-investment codification (e.g., code 705101 for share-capital acquisition); the beneficiary French SAS must file a Banque de France direct-investment declaration, and a prior French FDI authorisation is required for non-EU acquirers of control or a 25% voting threshold in the semiconductor sector under Décret n° 2019-1590. Remittance instructions must include the full legal name of the SAS, its SIREN/SIRET identifiers, the nature-of-payment field (remittance information in field 70) stating SUBSCRIBED CAPITAL INCREASE or SHAREHOLDER LOAN, and such inbound funds are subject to bank-side AML pre-clearance, verification against the corporate capital-resolution register, and an anti-money-laundering declaration where applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for outbound fabless disbursements are SWIFT MT103 high-value wire transfers for IP-core licence fees, design-service payments and foundry disbursements, using the relevant Banque de France balance-of-payments service/trade codes (e.g., licence-fee code 265U). For equipment or material procurement requiring a documentary instrument, Commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600 and standby LCs are available through the French bank's trade-finance desks; documents-against-payment and documents-against-acceptance collections provide supplementary rails. EUR disbursements clear through SEPA/SEPA Instant, while USD disbursements clear via the French bank's US correspondent on CHIPS or Fedwire; all outbound instructions must conform to the bank's Standard Settlement Instructions and include sanctioned-party screening before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forward contracts (change à terme) executed with ACPR/AMF-licensed credit institutions under MiFID II permissions, applied strictly to projected royalty and foundry payment exposures and eligible for IFRS 9 hedge accounting
Foreign-exchange swaps (swap de change) for shorter-dated liquidity alignment and roll-forward of contractual maturities
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps used for long-term synthetic EUR/USD matching of IP-licence and debt-service cash flows
Vanilla FX put and call options on a premium-payment basis for asymmetric protection of large USD licence receivables

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — legally permissible under French law, though of limited practical utility given full EUR/USD onshore convertibility; reserved for where a counterparty's jurisdiction requires NDF settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of earnings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or other body designated in the SAS articles; no government filing for the approval itself
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A court may order the company to approve the accounts, including under penalty payments; failure to approve does not by itself trigger automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce), through the national business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The president of the commercial court may issue an injunction to file. A company representative may face a fine of up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat offenses. No fixed automatic strike-off period applies solely for late accounts filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and applicable schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year close, ordinarily by the second working day after 1 May, subject to the current filing timetable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, potentially 40% after formal notice and 80% in specified cases, plus late-payment interest; additional penalties may apply for omissions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT returns and payment, if the company is VAT-registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly under the applicable normal regime; annual summary filing may apply under the simplified regime, with payments and return due on the prescribed dates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment may trigger surcharges, late-payment interest, and assessment based on available information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information update, if a reportable change occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the national business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the company becomes aware of a change requiring an update; no annual confirmation is required if information remains unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate, current information may result in criminal penalties for responsible persons and court orders; no automatic strike-off timeline applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of these thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Separate group and control-related rules can require an auditor at lower subsidiary thresholds or in other specified circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Commercial Code and ANC accounting regulations. IFRS is not generally required for an unlisted SAS's individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no routine annual UBO confirmation filing. The SAS must file an update within 30 days after a reportable change in beneficial ownership or relevant particulars. Shareholder transfers must be recorded in the company's securities movement and individual shareholder-account records; update the UBO filing only if the change affects reportable UBO information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Shareholder securities accounts and securities movement register, maintained at the company's registered office or by its authorized service provider
Minutes and written decisions of the president and shareholders, as applicable, maintained with the company's corporate records
Accounting books and supporting records required by French law; a separate statutory register of directors is not generally required for a French SAS

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 100-500 per year, depending on location and services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-8,000 per year for a straightforward SAS; complexity, group reporting, and scope may increase fees

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax on taxable profits under Article 219 of the French Tax Code (Code général des impôts).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small companies may qualify for a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to applicable capital ownership, turnover and paid-in-capital conditions. The French research tax credit generally equals 30% of eligible research expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to statutory eligibility and documentation. Qualifying innovation-related regimes, including the patent box regime, may tax eligible net intellectual-property income at 10%, subject to nexus and qualifying-asset requirements. The headline rate may be reduced by applicable tax credits, including the research tax credit, but credits do not automatically reduce the statutory taxable-income rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward under French law. Utilization in a taxable year is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding financial year and capped at the lower of the preceding year's profit and EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), filed electronically through the French Tax Administration professional portal at impots.gouv.fr/espace professionnel, generally using the EDI-TDFC electronic data interchange channel through an authorized provider. Financial statements and tax schedules generally include Forms 2050-SD through 2059-G-SD, as applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, with corporate income tax instalments generally paid quarterly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the standard deadline is the second business day following 1 May of the following year. Corporate income tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December. The final balance is generally due on the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, principal business activity, financial year dates and tax-consolidation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer unless it operates a French permanent establishment or otherwise has French taxable presence. The French SAS remains the filing entity and must report its French legal and tax identifiers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss determined under French corporate income tax rules after accounting-to-tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income and expenses attributable to the French SAS. Payments to non-resident related parties must be supported by arm's-length evidence, beneficial-ownership analysis and applicable withholding-tax treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation differences, tax-exempt income and prior-year tax attributes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude shareholder-level income and expenses that do not belong to the French company. Document adjustments for foreign taxes, withholding taxes, grants, royalties and intercompany charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of carried-forward losses, current-year losses and carryback claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a non-resident parent or affiliate cannot be used by the French SAS unless a specific French tax-consolidation or statutory regime applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Forms 2050-SD to 2057-SD, balance sheet and profit-and-loss schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed assets, liabilities, equity, turnover, operating expenses, financial income and financial expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS's statutory accounts. Foreign-currency balances must be translated in accordance with French accounting rules and supporting intercompany reconciliations must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals of fixed assets, securities and other capital items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French participation-exemption and long-term capital-gain rules only where statutory conditions are satisfied. A non-resident shareholder's disposal of SAS shares is separately analyzed under French domestic law and the applicable treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning subsidiaries, participations and qualifying ownership interests.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign subsidiaries and related entities accurately. Ownership information must be consistent with corporate records, beneficial-owner filings and transfer-pricing disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research tax credit, family tax credit, apprenticeship-related credits and other eligible credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign ownership does not itself prevent a French SAS from claiming French tax credits, but the underlying expenditure, French activities, personnel and technical documentation must satisfy the relevant statutory conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate income tax, credits, instalments, withholding offsets and final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding tax suffered abroad is not automatically creditable against French corporate income tax. Relief depends on French law, the relevant treaty and the legal character of the foreign tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of controlled transactions, methods, amounts and counterparties where the statutory reporting threshold or qualifying group conditions apply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border related-party transactions involving the French SAS, including semiconductor design services, IP licensing, cost-sharing, financing and procurement arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2067-SD, statement of non-deductible financial expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certain interest, related-party financing and other financial charges subject to French limitation rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose related-party debt, implicit or explicit guarantees, thin-capitalization effects and interest limitation adjustments. Maintain loan agreements, cash-flow evidence and debt-capacity analysis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% in cases of deliberate non-compliance after formal notice and potentially 80% in cases involving fraudulent conduct or abusive concealment. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules and available relief. Repeated or aggravated failures may trigger separate tax-fraud, accounting, withholding-tax or transfer-pricing penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2572-SD (corporate income tax payment balance) and electronic payment through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal or authorized EDI payment channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly instalments and annual balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December. The final balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month after financial year-end, with a specific May deadline for a 31 December year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2572-SD, tax base and gross liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax liability calculated from the filed annual return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS's French corporate income tax liability only; do not offset a foreign parent's tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly instalments already paid during the relevant financial year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile payment references and bank debits with the French SAS tax account before submission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible French tax credits and legally creditable withholding amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim foreign withholding credits without treaty or domestic-law support and documentary evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net amount due or refundable after instalments and eligible credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the French SAS's French bank account and tax-account payment mandate are active; shareholder funding must be recorded separately from tax payment mechanics.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally triggers late-payment interest and a 5% surcharge for late payment of tax, subject to statutory exceptions. Material underpayments may also lead to reassessment, a 10% filing surcharge, higher penalties for deliberate conduct and collection measures.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions and treaty relief. Qualifying distributions to an eligible EU parent may be exempt under the French implementation of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring qualifying ownership, holding-period and anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, identify the recipient, beneficial owner, residence state, legal form, ownership percentage, holding period and applicable treaty article. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's tax authority and collect any required treaty-relief form or self-certification. Apply the reduced rate only where procedural and substantive conditions are satisfied. If relief at source is unavailable or uncertain, withhold at the domestic rate and seek a refund from the French Tax Administration using the applicable non-resident refund procedure. Maintain board resolutions, dividend vouchers, ownership evidence, residence certificates and beneficial-ownership records.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments to non-residents are generally subject to a 25% French withholding tax under domestic law, potentially increased to 75% for payments to specified non-cooperative jurisdictions or territories. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to rates ranging from 0% to 15%, depending on the treaty and beneficial-owner conditions. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions apply, including specified non-cooperative-jurisdiction rules, anti-abuse provisions and special payment categories. Treaty rates must be determined from the specific recipient jurisdiction; no universal treaty rate exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million. A French entity or French tax group generally falls within the full transfer-pricing documentation regime where its annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets reach at least EUR 400 million, or where it is associated with an entity meeting the statutory EUR 400 million threshold. The full regime generally requires a Master File and Local File. A transfer-pricing summary filing on Form 2257-SD may apply at lower thresholds, commonly including EUR 150 million turnover or gross assets or qualifying group conditions. French entities below the full threshold must still apply the arm's-length principle and may be required to provide adequate documentation on request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a separate, generally applicable UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Economic substance is nevertheless material under French transfer-pricing rules, the abuse-of-law doctrine, the principal-purpose and anti-abuse rules, controlled foreign company rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, interest limitation rules and general anti-avoidance principles. A French SAS conducting semiconductor architecture and IP licensing should maintain qualified personnel, decision-making capacity, technical records, functional risk control, development evidence, premises or operational infrastructure appropriate to its activities, and contemporaneous ownership and exploitation records for intellectual property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing revenue, inflating deductions, using false invoices, omitting taxable distributions, falsifying transfer-pricing records or submitting materially false corporate tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, tax surcharges generally up to 40% for deliberate conduct and up to 80% for fraudulent or abusive conduct. Aggravated tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, increasing in specified aggravated cases to up to 7 years and EUR 3 million. Corporate fines may be multiplied under French criminal-law rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, tax-payment liability in cases of fraudulent or seriously negligent management, civil damages, management bans and asset-seizure measures. Travel restrictions are not automatic; imprisonment requires criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and hidden profit distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, design fees, cost-sharing contributions or financing charges; shifting French-developed semiconductor IP without compensation; or using an unsupported low-tax principal structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional corporate tax, interest, transfer-pricing reassessment, potential 40% or 80% tax surcharge, documentation-related penalties and possible withholding tax on recharacterized payments. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may attract a penalty generally linked to the higher of a statutory minimum and a percentage of the corrected transaction amount, subject to statutory caps.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for breach of management duties, criminal exposure where falsification or fraud is proven, and personal tax-payment liability in cases of fraudulent management. Veil piercing is exceptional and fact-dependent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared permanent establishment or artificial residency position
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a foreign principal or contract manufacturer while French personnel habitually negotiate or conclude contracts, perform core DEMPE functions, control risks or conduct the enterprise's central business from France without appropriate French taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French corporate income tax, business taxes, withholding taxes, payroll and VAT exposure where applicable, interest, late-filing surcharges and potential permanent-establishment reassessment under domestic law and the applicable treaty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be liable for misleading filings, concealment and unpaid tax where their conduct is intentional or seriously negligent. Criminal liability depends on proof of fraud; travel bans and imprisonment are not automatic consequences of a tax reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, corruption and misuse of company funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing royalties, consulting fees, distributor commissions or capital payments through opaque entities, nominees or personal accounts; disguising bribes as technical services; or accepting proceeds derived from criminal conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering may carry up to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of up to EUR 375,000, with aggravated cases carrying up to 10 years and EUR 750,000. Corruption offences carry separate and potentially more severe criminal sanctions. Corporate criminal fines, confiscation and prohibition orders may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners and employees may be prosecuted personally. Asset confiscation, management bans and civil restitution are possible. Travel restrictions may be ordered by a court; imprisonment requires conviction or may arise pre-trial under judicial-control rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify or update the beneficial owner, using nominee shareholders to conceal control, providing inconsistent ownership information, or failing to maintain customer and counterparty due diligence for high-risk payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative, civil and criminal consequences may include filing injunctions, fines, refusal or suspension of account or transaction services, director-management sanctions and prosecution where the conduct supports fraud, money laundering or false declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives may be personally liable for knowingly false filings or obstruction. Civil restitution and management prohibitions may apply; travel bans or imprisonment require a specific judicial basis and are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful IP royalty or technology-transfer structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming ownership of IP developed by French personnel without proper assignments, charging royalties without demonstrable IP value, failing to maintain R&D and DEMPE evidence, or using a conduit company lacking beneficial ownership and substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, denial of deductions or patent-box treatment, withholding-tax liability, interest, penalties, potential abuse-of-law recharacterization and civil IP claims. Unlawful export-control or technology-transfer conduct may create separate criminal or administrative exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability for unauthorized exploitation, breach of fiduciary duties or deliberate tax abuse. Criminal liability arises where fraud, counterfeiting, corruption or other specific offences are established.
